notes: On 8 June 2025, hundreds to thousands of pro-immigration demonstrators gathered outside the Metropolitan Detention Center in downtown Los Angeles - Central (California) to denounce ICE deportations, the last two days of clashes between demonstrators and federal agents and local police, and the activation of the National Guard. The demonstration likely included members of the Mexican community (based on the presence of Mexican flags). Demonstrators shouted insults at National Guard troops forming a skirmish line behind plastic riot shields. Other law enforcement officials were also on scene and it was not immediately clear which service began firing tear gas at the demonstrators. Police then began firing crowd-control munitions and pepper spray at the demonstrators. A New York Times analysis of multiple videos from the intersection of East Temple and North Alameda Streets found that two police officers separately shot two demonstrators in the face and head, respectively, with 40mm impact sponge rounds, severely injuring them. This breached Department protocol, which states that sponge rounds should only be used on specific individuals who pose an 'immediate threat to safety,' that the rounds shall not be fired at the head unless lethal force is authorized, and that the rounds cannot be used to disperse crowds. A Mounted Unit officer subsequently trampled the latter demonstrator with their horse and beat them with a baton. While journalists reported from the front line of demonstrators with identifiable press markings, police officers separately hit three journalists with 40mm impact sponge rounds, and also a British news photographer was shot in the thigh and had to be taken to the hospital and operated on. Demonstrators also vandalized a KTLA news van with paint. Demonstrators then spilled onto the 101 freeway southbound and the overpass above it, forming a makeshift barricade to block traffic and facing off with a skirmish line of Guards and California Highway Patrol officers and their vehicles. Demonstrators threw chunks of concrete, rocks, soda cans, electric scooters, and fireworks at the units. Police detained one person for throwing a Molotov cocktail at police and another for ramming a motorcycle into a line of officers. Police ultimately arrested 19 people. At least four self-driving Waymo cars were set on fire and exploded intermittently as the electric vehicles burned. By evening, police issued an unlawful assembly order and largely secured the few blocks around the freeway and Metropolitan Detention Center. In the evening, police shot a New York Times reporter in the torso with a crowd control munition. Several downtown Los Angeles businesses were looted and vandalized overnight (coded separately).

source: Block Club Chicago; Bluesky; CBS News; CNN; Fox32; Left Coast Right Watch; NBC 26; News2Share; On the Scene; The TRiiBE; Twitter; US Press Freedom Tracker; WGN Channel 9
notes: On 27 September 2025, about 100 demonstrators rallied outside an ICE processing facility in Broadview (Illinois) to protest Trump and ICE's 'Operation Midway Blitz,' as well as to protest claims of inhumane treatment within the facility. Demonstrators also chanted 'F*ck Trump.' Dozens of ICE agents fired pepper balls, rubber bullets, flash grenades, and tear gas at the demonstrators, who obstructed law enforcement by attempting to block vehicles from passing with their bodies. ICE agents chased at least two demonstrators and arrested them after they were warned to clear the street to allow vehicles to leave the facility. ICE later threw gas cannisters into the crowd. Those present included members of Revcom (Revolutionary Communist Party), Corps for the Emancipation of Humanity Chicago and the Revolutionary Black Panther Party. ICE agents also hit at least five journalists with pepper balls or tear gas and arrested at least one journalist while they claimed they were merely observing the demonstration. A journalist with Zuma Press was struck with pepper balls several times and says he was directly targeted despite being a known journalist. Another journalist with Humanizing Through Stories was affected by tear gas and lost a camera lens. A third journalist with Unraveled Press was tackled and arrested by federal agents for standing in the road, despite his claim that he was given no time to move. Journalists with CBS News Chicago were also affected by tear gas. Another journalist with WBBM-TV was hit and claimed they were directly targeted with a pepper ball while driving to the facility. An independent photojournalist and a photojournalist with WLS-TV were shot with pepper balls and tear gas. 11 demonstrators were arrested. Five demonstrators were charged with impeding, resisting, and assaulting federal officers. All five fought physically with agents, with one ICE agent suffering a minor thumb injury as a result. Two demonstrators were arrested after ICE agents found them to be armed with loaded semi-automatic pistols. Police presence included CBP, ATF, ICE agents, and local police.
